minutes.headline: Parks Commission voted to ask DPW to finish the Marshall Pond pocket park and resurface the track; accepted Little League's spring payment.
minutes.summary: Meeting opened with public anger over cancelled summer recreation programs, the best soccer camp cancellation over a school field fee, and permit questions. The commission then voted on lifeguard hires, a Marshall Park priorities motion, and Little League's spring fees. Porta-potties, the dumpster, the dog policy and the Marshall Park master plan were discussed and deferred to a July 14 reconvened meeting.

public_comment.topic: Town beach part-time employee asked the commission to allow swim lesson classes of 12 students to clear the waitlist.

Five questions on the recreation program: temporary replacement for the director, busy schedule, camp locations not secured, the Marshall Park option, and Board of Health permits; also the inconvenience of last-minute cancellation.
Follow-up on whether running camps are cleared by the Board of Health; also said the school charges her Girl Scout troop for meeting space.
A member of the public urged focus on planned programs over the next six to eight weeks and earlier communication; suggested offering cancelled registrants alternative programs.

what_happened.line: The Parks Commission voted to recommend that the DPW director move ahead with the Marshall Pond pocket park and cosmetic resurfacing of the Marshall Park track.
The commission voted to accept Little League's payment as payment in full for the spring 2021 season; Little League had paid at last year's fees.
The commission voted to recommend hiring two lifeguards for the town beach for the 2021 season.
Public comment opened the meeting with objections to cancelled summer programs, including a camp cancelled over a school field rental fee, and questions about permits.
Porta-potties, the dumpster, the dog policy and the Marshall Park master plan were deferred to a meeting reconvened July 14.

why_it_matters: Summer recreation for families depends on which programs actually run, and the cancellations show how a school field fee or a missing permit can end a camp on short notice.
Which park projects come first, and who pays for upkeep at the three major parks, was left open, so work such as Marshall Park and portable toilets has no decision yet.
watch_next: Reconvened meeting on July 14 at 6:30 pm by Zoom, with the Marshall Park master plan and project priorities on the agenda.
Dog policy draft due for the last Wednesday meeting of July.

reconciliation.summary: The two records agree on all three votes and on most decisions. The differences are caption-garbled names, plus detail and public-comment items that only one record has. No transfers appear in either record, and I found no substantive conflict on a vote or an amount.
